neighbours.label: ' for' after a verb of pleading or searching for something badly needed (begged for bread, prayed for rain, searched for shelter)
fire: The hungry children pleaded for food outside the bakery.
During the drought the whole town prayed for rain every evening.
The shipwrecked crew scanned the horizon and hoped for rescue.
As the storm closed in, the climbers hunted for shelter among the rocks.
The wounded soldier cried out for water in the night.
Thousands of families queued for bread during the siege.
The exhausted swimmers shouted for help from the reef.
After the earthquake the survivors dug through rubble and begged for medicine.
quiet: The hungry children ate their food outside the bakery.
During the drought the whole town stayed indoors for weeks.
The shipwrecked crew had sailed for Lisbon in March.
As the storm closed in, the climbers rested for an hour among the rocks.
The wounded soldier slept for most of the night.
Thousands of families paid for bread with ration cards.
The exhausted swimmers thanked the lifeguard for his work.
After the earthquake the engineers inspected the bridge for cracks.

notes: Card: function words leading into a hoped-for relief (offering to, awaited the rescue ship, conserve grain for); the - pole's output promotes survival / recovery / rescue words. Probes are weak: prayed for 0.25, begged for 0.25, searched for 0.35, waited for 0.19; purpose and longing sentences 0.02-0.05. Expect a borderline result.
